title: Australian Passport Photo Online or at Home: What Is Allowed?
metaTitle: Australian Passport Photo Online or at Home? What Is Allowed
metaDescription: Can you make an Australian passport photo online or at home? Passports need 2 dye-sublimation prints on 200 gsm glossy paper. Here is what you can do.
excerpt: An honest answer to the online, free and at-home question: what the Passport Office allows, why home prints fail, and when an online photo tool is genuinely useful.
keywords: take your own passport photo australia
keyTakeaways: You cannot upload a digital photo for an Australian passport.
You need 2 colour prints made by dye sublimation, on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm.
The Passport Office recommends a professional provider, not online services or apps.
Online tools are useful for checking a photo, and for digital uploads such as some visa and citizenship applications.
intro: **Quick answer:** You cannot use a home or online digital photo for an Australian passport. You need 2 professional colour prints made by dye sublimation, on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm. Online tools are still useful for checking a photo, and for digital uploads such as some visa and citizenship applications.

> **Important:** The Australian Passport Office recommends a professional passport photo provider and does not recommend online photo services or apps. Use our tool to check or prepare a photo, but always confirm it meets the official guidelines before you apply.
**[Check my photo with the Australian passport photo checker →](/australian-passport-photo-checker)**
We make an online photo tool, so we could tell you otherwise. But a photo that does not meet the rules costs you time, so here is exactly what is allowed.

sections.heading: Can I take my own Australian passport photo?

subsections.heading: What the Passport Office recommends
content: The Passport Office recommends a professional passport photo provider, such as a post office, professional photographer, camera store, some pharmacies or some chain stores.
It does not recommend online photo services or mobile apps.

subsections.heading: What the rules say about print quality
content: Your photos must be good-quality colour prints made by dye sublimation, not by an inkjet printer. The paper must be heavy-weight and glossy, at least 200 gsm.
These print rules are the main reason a home photo is hard to use.

subsections.heading: What you can still do yourself
content: You can learn the rules, practise your pose and check a test photo before you visit a provider. That helps you spot problems like glasses, hair over your eyes or a tilted head.
You can also check the prints you get back against the [Australian passport photo requirements](/guides/australian-passport-photo-requirements).

sections.heading: Can I upload a digital photo for an Australian passport?

subsections.heading: Why passports need printed photos
content: The Passport Office asks for 2 printed photos. Its guidelines set the print method and the paper, so a digital file on its own does not meet them.
Always check the official guidelines on the day you apply, in case the process changes.

subsections.heading: What dye sublimation means in simple terms
content: Dye sublimation is a printing method that uses heat to turn solid dye into a gas, which then sets into the paper. It gives smooth colour without dots or streaks.
Many photo kiosks and professional photo printers use it. Most home printers do not.

subsections.heading: Why an inkjet print is not accepted
content: The guidelines say photos must not be printed on an inkjet printer. Inkjet prints can show lines, streaks and ink marks, which are all listed as unacceptable.
They can also smudge or fade, which makes the face harder to check.

sections.heading: Can I print passport photos at home?

subsections.heading: Home inkjet printing and why it fails
content: Most home printers are inkjet printers. Even with good photo paper, an inkjet print does not meet the dye-sublimation rule.
Printing a sheet of photos at home and cutting them out is very unlikely to work for an Australian passport.

subsections.heading: Paper type and weight (glossy, minimum 200 gsm)
content: Passport photos need heavy-weight, glossy paper of at least 200 gsm. Normal printer paper is far lighter than this.
Paper weight alone is not enough, though. The print method must still be dye sublimation.

subsections.heading: What a professional provider does differently
content: A professional provider uses suitable lighting, a plain background and a printer that makes dye-sublimation prints on the right paper. They also print to the correct size, so you do not need to trim anything.
Many can retake the photo straight away if something is wrong.

sections.heading: Why does the Passport Office not recommend online photo services?

subsections.heading: Identity fraud risk
content: The Passport Office warns that online photo services and mobile apps may put you at risk of identity fraud. You are sending a clear photo of your face to a business you may know little about.
Only use services you trust, and read their privacy policy before you upload.

subsections.heading: Photo quality problems
content: Online services and apps often edit photos: smoothing skin, removing backgrounds or adjusting colours. Retouching and edited backgrounds are both listed as unacceptable.
Photos taken at home are also more likely to have shadows, distortion or the wrong head size.

subsections.heading: How to choose a safe provider
content: Choose a provider that takes passport photos regularly and knows the Australian rules. Ask whether they print by dye sublimation on 200 gsm glossy paper.
Our [where to get an Australian passport photo](/guides/where-to-get-australian-passport-photo) guide lists the types of providers and what to ask them.

sections.heading: When is an online photo tool useful?

subsections.heading: Checking size, head height and background before you print
content: An online checker can tell you if your head is too big or too small, if the background has shadows, or if you are wearing glasses. That is worth knowing before you pay for prints.
You can also photograph a test shot at home to practise your pose.

subsections.heading: Preparing a digital photo for a visa or citizenship upload
content: Some applications do accept digital photos. A citizenship application made online needs a JPEG file, and some visa applications ask for a photo upload.

See our [Australia visa photo requirements](/guides/australia-visa-photo-requirements) and [Australian citizenship photo requirements](/guides/australian-citizenship-photo-requirements) guides for those rules.

subsections.heading: What our tool does not do
content: Our tool cannot make a dye-sublimation print, and it cannot promise that the Passport Office will accept your photo.
It is a check, not an approval. Officers make the final decision.

sections.heading: Where can I get the right prints?

subsections.heading: Post offices, professional photographers and chain stores
content: The Passport Office lists post offices, professional photographers, some large chain stores with printing facilities, many camera stores and some pharmacies as providers.
It does not endorse any particular business.

subsections.heading: What to ask the provider to confirm
content:
- 2 identical colour prints
- 35-40 mm wide x 45-50 mm high, with the head 32-36 mm from chin to crown
- dye-sublimation printing on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm
- no retouching

subsections.heading: Australian Passport Office
content: - [Passport photo guidelines](https://www.passports.gov.au/PhotoGuidelines): print type, paper weight, provider advice and the warning about online services and apps

subsections.heading: Department of Home Affairs
content: - [Photo requirements for citizenship applications](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/citizenship/apply-for-citizenship/prepare-application/photo-requirements): the digital JPEG rules for online citizenship applications

subsections.heading: Last updated
content: Last updated: 21 November 2026. We checked these rules against the official pages on this date.
Rules and file limits change, so we review this page every 3 months. Always read the official page on the day you apply.

faq.question: Is there a free Australian passport photo online?
faq.answer: There are free online tools, but none can give you a photo that meets the passport print rules. Australian passports need 2 dye-sublimation prints on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm. A free tool can help you check a photo, but you still need a professional provider for the prints.

faq.question: Can I use a digital passport photo for an Australian passport?
faq.answer: No. The Passport Office asks for 2 printed photos, made by dye sublimation on heavy glossy paper. A digital file on its own does not meet these rules. Digital photos are used for some other applications, such as online citizenship applications and some visa uploads.

faq.question: Can I print my Australian passport photo at home?
faq.answer: It is very unlikely to work. Most home printers are inkjet printers, and the Passport Office does not accept inkjet prints. Photos must be dye-sublimation prints on glossy paper of at least 200 gsm. A post office or professional photographer can make prints that meet these rules.

faq.question: Can I use my phone to take an Australian passport photo?
faq.answer: You can use a phone for a practice shot or a pre-check, but the Passport Office does not recommend apps, and the final photos must be professional dye-sublimation prints. Phone photos taken too close also distort the face, which is listed as unacceptable.

faq.question: Is an app passport photo accepted in Australia?
faq.answer: The Passport Office does not recommend mobile apps or online photo services, and warns they may put you at risk of identity fraud. App photos are often edited, and editing is not allowed. Use a professional provider for passport prints, and use apps only for checking.

cta.title: Check a photo before you print it
cta.text: Our checker tests head height, background, lighting and glasses. It cannot make a passport print, and a pass is not an approval.
